title: The Periodic Table
seo_title: Grade 8 Science: The Periodic Table Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: The periodic table arranges elements by atomic number into groups and periods; elements in a group have similar properties; metals, non-metals and metalloids. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 8, Quarter 2: Science of Materials)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 2: Science of Materials): organizing the periodic table, groups and valence electrons, families of elements, periodic trends and trends in properties. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Elements in a group have the same number of valence electrons.
key_sub: Atomic radius increases down a group and decreases across a period.
body_html:
How to think about it

The periodic table arranges elements by atomic number. Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties because they have the same number of valence electrons: alkali metals (group 1), halogens (group 17) and noble gases (group 18).

Across a period the nuclear charge increases, so atoms get smaller and ionization energy and electronegativity increase. Down a group extra energy levels are added, so atoms get bigger and ionization energy decreases.

Example

Which is larger, Na or Cl?

Same period; Cl has more protons pulling the electrons in.

Answer: Na

Example

Why are the noble gases unreactive?

Look at the outer energy level.

Answer: their outer energy level is full

Common mistakes

  • Thinking atoms get bigger across a period.
  • Mixing up groups (columns) and periods (rows).
  • Thinking the halogens are metals.
